activity.notes: Áedán mac Gabráin was a historically attested ruler of the Gaelic kingdom later known as Dál Riata. The surviving annalistic and hagiographic chronologies vary slightly, with accession around 574/576 and death around 608/609, so ATLAS records c.574–c.609 rather than false exactness.

sources.title: From Caledonia to Pictland: Scotland to 795 — Chapter 5
sources.citation_text: The scholarly study describes Áedán son of Gabrán as the first early Scottish king whose career can be reconstructed in narrative form and places his accession around 576.

sources.title: Áedán mac Gabráin
sources.citation_text: The compiled chronology, drawing on Irish annals and Adomnán, gives Áedán's reign over Dál Riata from about 574 until about 609.
